title: Edit transcription
subtitle: Adjust subtitle text and display timing.

inspector.heading: Inspector
inspector.bulkHelp: Applies the changes you make here to every subtitle you have checked in the list. Use the list view to pick the targets.
inspector.emptyHint: Click a row in the list or a block in the timeline below

bulk.title: Bulk editing
bulk.body: Tick the checkboxes on the left to select several rows and the Inspector switches to Bulk edit, letting you change text colour, size, outline, shadow and more for all of them at once. To undo, use the Undo button in the toolbar (Ctrl+Z). Each setting you change is one step, so a single undo reverts every selected row (change colour and size and that is two undos). Selection is separate from undo — undoing does not clear your selection.

preview.title: Which settings the list shows
preview.body: The subtitle text shown in the list reflects your Inspector settings. Applied: font, text colour and opacity, outline colour and thickness, shadow, uppercasing, the background box and the keyword-emphasis colour. Not applied: font size, emphasis scale, rotation, karaoke, animation, and position and margins. Font size is scaled down to fit the column, and a line too long even then is cut off with an ellipsis. Check the preview and the exported video for the final look.

styleCell.outlineWidthBgMinNote: Keep this at 1 or more while the background box is on. The box is drawn by thickening the outline, so at 0 the export carries no background at all.
styleCell.lineSpacingHint: Gap between the lines of a multi-line caption, as a percentage of the font size. 0% is the default.
styleCell.positionHint: Absolute position in video pixels. Entering a value pins the caption at that coordinate. Use "Reset position" to return to the aligned position.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsOn: Speech timing: colors each word as it was actually spoken, using the timings captured at transcription.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsOff: Speech timing: off. The display time is split evenly across the characters.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsNoWords: Speech timing: this subtitle has no per-word timings from transcription (imported from SRT, added by hand, and so on). The display time is split evenly instead.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsTextEdited: Speech timing: the text was edited, so it no longer lines up with the recorded timings. The display time is split evenly instead. Restore the text, or use "Reset row", to bring it back.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsTimeEdited: Speech timing: the display time was changed, so the link to the audio is broken. The display time is split evenly instead. Undo, or use "Reset row", to bring it back.
styleCell.karaokeWordTimingsBulk: Speech timing: applies to every selected row. Even when on, rows with no per-word timings — or whose text or display time was edited — stay on the even split.

scope.title: What MOJIOKO can and cannot do
scope.body: MOJIOKO adds subtitles to a video you have already finished editing — it does not edit the video itself. You can only work inside the original video's running time, and you cannot join another video or add audio or images. Concatenate several clips into one, and mix in music, sound effects or graphics, in a video editor first, then load the result here. Note that subtitles sharing a row and overlapping in time also overlap on screen, which can make them hard to read.

trim.title: Trimming
trim.body: In and Out are placed at the playhead position when you press them. Once both are set, Run becomes available and removes that span from the video itself, rippling the rest forward to fill the gap (with only one point set, Run stays disabled). Placing Out at or before In is refused as you set it. Before you commit, press the same button again or use the clear button beside them. Afterwards, click the scissor marker left on the timeline to undo the trim — with nested trims the outermost goes first, and removing it reveals the marker inside it.

snap.title: Snap
snap.body: With Snap on, dragging a subtitle edge lines it up with nearby subtitle edges and ruler ticks. Turn it off to place edges freely.

layers.title: Rows are stacking order
layers.body: A timeline row is the subtitle's stacking order. The bottom row sits furthest back and higher rows draw in front. Rows do not appear on their own when subtitles overlap in time — drag a block up or down to change its row, or use Stacking order in the inspector. Subtitles that share a row and overlap in time overlap on it; move one to another row to separate them.

emphasisPicker.title: Select characters to emphasise
emphasisPicker.description: Click the characters you want to emphasise. Drag to select a run, or shift-click to extend the selection.
emphasisPicker.editNote: Emphasis follows your text edits automatically. A line break falling inside an emphasised run does not clear it — both lines stay emphasised. It is cleared only where the emphasised characters are deleted or rewritten, or where the same text ends up appearing more than once and can no longer be told apart.
